headline: A new law lets the VA provide a casket or urn for certain veterans whose next of kin cannot be found, for burial in national or grant-supported state or tribal veterans cemeteries.
what_it_does: The law allows the Department of Veterans Affairs to pay for a casket or urn when it cannot identify a deceased veteran's next of kin. It applies only if other resources for the casket or urn are not available. The burial can be in a VA national cemetery or in a state or tribal veterans cemetery that received a VA grant to establish, expand, or improve it.

who_it_affects.group: Deceased veterans with no identifiable next of kin
who_it_affects.how: Their burial may include a casket or urn furnished by the VA when other resources are not available.

who_it_affects.group: State and tribal veterans cemeteries that received VA grants
who_it_affects.how: They may be used as burial sites for veterans whose caskets or urns the VA furnishes.
The agency gains authority to furnish caskets or urns in these situations.

when_it_takes_effect: The law became effective upon enactment on December 14, 2016.
